blocks.prompt: 1. Find the \(8^{\text{th}}\) term of the arithmetico-geometric sequence, where the arithmetic part is \(1, 4, 7, \ldots\) and the geometric part is \(5, 10, 20, \ldots\)
blocks.explanation:
Each term of an A.G.P. is an A.P. term times the matching G.P. term.
So the 8th term is (8th term of \(1, 4, 7, \ldots\)) \(\times\) (8th term of \(5, 10, 20, \ldots\)).
Plan: find each 8th term with its own formula, then multiply.
steps:
Given: A.P. part \(1, 4, 7, \ldots\) (\(a = 1, d = 3\)); G.P. part \(5, 10, 20, \ldots\) (\(b = 5, r = 2\))
To find: the 8th term \(T_8\).
Method: The \(n\)th term of an A.G.P. is (\(n\)th term of the A.P. part) \(\times\) (\(n\)th term of the G.P. part): \(T_n = [a + (n - 1)d]\,br^{n-1}\).

8th term of the A.P. part
\[a_8 = a + 7d\]
\[= 1 + 7(3) = 22\]
Why: \(a_n = a + (n - 1)d\); from the 1st to the 8th term \(d = 4 - 1 = 3\) is added 7 times.

8th term of the G.P. part
\[b_8 = br^{7}\]
\[= 5 \cdot 2^{7}\]
\[= 5 \times 128 = 640\]
Why: \(b_n = br^{n-1}\) with \(r = 10/5 = 2\); the power is \(8 - 1 = 7\).

Multiply the two 8th terms
\[T_8 = a_8 \times b_8\]
\[= 22 \times 640\]
\[= 14080\]
Why: The A.G.P. term is the product of the matching terms; \(22 \times 640 = 12800 + 1280\).

Check by listing
\[1, 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22\]
\[5, 10, 20, \ldots, 320, 640\]
Why: Writing out both parts, the 8th entries are 22 and 640, as found.
